proposals.evidence: DEDR4782 explicitly gives Tamil māṅkāy and Telugu mã̄gāyu mango fruit beside mā/māvu mango; DEDR1459 gives kāy/kāyi/kāyu fruit. The complete survey māṅgāy/māṅgāyɨ/māvaṅkai/māṅgekāyɨ responses are ordered mango + fruit compounds, with compound nasal and ordinary vowel/voicing variants retained.

proposals.evidence: Ordered sesame + oil: DEDR854 explicitly gives Tamil eṇ ṇey gingelly oil and related Malayalam eṇṇa/Kannada eṇṇe, while3746 gives ney oil. These lexicalized eṇṇey/eṇṇa/eṇṇe survey responses are analysed with both historical constituents; their generalized survey gloss oil and all dialect transcriptions remain unchanged.

proposals.evidence: Ordered ground + gram: DEDR3676 nilam/nela earth/ground and1120 kaṭalai/kaṭala gram. Survey nila-/nela-kaḍala(i) groundnut transparently contains both constituents; its modern groundnut designation is retained as a compound, not conflated with the botanical gram referent of1120.

proposals.evidence: Ordered male + child components, comparing the contracted Tamil formation. Sri Lanka Educational Publications Department, Tamil11, printed p.112 (https://noolaham.net/project/795/79443/79443.pdf), visually verified, explicitly pairs āmpiḷai with āṇpiḷḷai in its colloquial/standard table. DEDR399 supplies āṇ male and4198 piḷḷai child. Survey contractions preserve these components; source vowel/rhotic variants remain unchanged, and borrowing versus shared formation across varieties is not resolved by this component analysis. See tamil-contracted-kinship-evidence.md.
